items.title: 52222_Marshall Royal oral history interview
items.q: He saved up his money and without a whole lot of outside financing, he built the Dunbar Hotel

ctx.x: And that was black-owned, was it not? (inaudible)?

-- and it was black-owned by a very prominent physician, Dr. Somerville (PHONETIC). He saved up his money and without a whole lot of outside financing, he built the Dunbar Hotel and it was a first-class hotel. He also, about a half-mile away from there, put up the following year an apartment house called the La Vada Apartments, which was named after his wife, whose name was Vada (PHONETIC) Somerville. They were two of the nicest buildings on the East Side of town. At that time, that was the -- one of the first…
